notes: bot v7: single-instance lock now verifies the lock owner's identity before honoring the lock. The v4-v6 lock only kill(pid,0)-checked the recorded pid; on device the recorded pid was recycled by an unrelated long-lived chroot process, so every watchdog respawn exited as 'already running' while no bot was alive. The lock payload is now JSON {pid, start} (legacy bare-pid locks still parse); a recorded owner is honored only if /proc/<pid>/cmdline has argv[0] containing node plus an argument exactly equal to the bot.js path, and the recorded /proc/<pid>/stat starttime (field 22) matches when present. Foreign, recycled, dead or unparsable locks are taken over with a '锁残留（pid X 非机器人进程），接管' log line; alive-but-unverifiable owners still conservatively block, and a genuine second instance still exits with '已有实例在运行'. All other bot behavior unchanged from v6: ranked candidate fallthrough (up to 3 candidates tried silently; dead_source, failed, blocked, or link-less candidates are skipped for the next; the group sees one searching message plus the final link or one honest all-sources-failed reply), empty-search retry (up to 2 re-runs at ~6s gaps), 21:00-23:59 Asia/Shanghai digest poster, message_id dedup, video-over-novel pick. Scripts v8: start_qqbot.sh now also aligns the quick-login account hardcoded in the in-container NapCat launcher before NapCat starts. install_env.sh generated /root/qqbot/start-napcat.sh at install time with the launch line './napcat.sh -q 3322592972' baked in; after the swap to 411649762 every stack start first tried quick login for the old account (flagged by QQ, no valid session), failed and fell back to a QR scan — a scan was demanded on every restart, while the old account had quick-logged reliably precisely because -q named its own account. The hook takes the current bot account (first entry of QQ_BOT_ACCOUNTS, 411649762): if the launcher's -q already names it, nothing happens; if it still names the stale 3322592972, the launcher is backed up once to start-napcat.sh.bak (an existing backup is never overwritten) and only the -q argument is rewritten via temp file + atomic mv (mode 755 preserved); a missing launcher or one without the -q pattern is logged and skipped, and no failure can block stack start. The scripts v7 OneBot-config seeding/self-healing for 411649762 is unchanged: missing per-account configs are seeded from the base onebot11.json; existing ones are health-checked (ws enable:true and port 3001) and left completely untouched when healthy, otherwise backed up to .bak and realigned to base; a missing base still only warns.
